2010_001_020310regmtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting agenda for Wednesday, February 3, 2010, at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, combines recognitions, curriculum reports, and the district's principal mid-year financial actions. Its central item is the 2009-10 Budget Amendment Resolution, which appropriates $136,562,590 in the General Fund, $7,614,554 in Special Revenue Funds, $18,749,640 in Debt Service Funds, $5,032,861 in the Capital Projects Fund, and $720,000 in the Internal Service Fund, with amended General Fund state revenue set at $65,916,278. The packet also carries January 2010 board minutes, results of a parent survey completed by 2,752 respondents, a $66,800.00 security management system award to MCMI, and a five-year budget forecast by Michael Adamczyk.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, Wednesday, February 3, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district masthead 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., except July and August.

**Recognitions**
North Central Association accreditation from the Advanced Accreditation Commission; the plaque goes to Stu Redpath, chair of the districtwide NCA process. The Troy Academy of Learning Leaders (TALL), in its second year with 14 teacher leaders, earned the 2009 "Best Practices in Human Resources" award from the Michigan Association of School Personnel Administrators, presented to Jasen Witt, assistant superintendent for human resources, at the December MASPA annual conference.

**Consent agenda (item 5)**
Minutes of the January 19, 2010 organizational meeting, the January 19, 2010 board meeting, and the January 22, 2010 board retreat. The organizational meeting (7:03 p.m. to 7:06 p.m.) adopted resolutions 10-001 through 10-004, all Yes 7 / No 0: Michael M. Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent-Business Services, as Treasurer for the 2010 calendar year; continued designation of the Superintendent as Deputy Secretary; Shelly Carrier for posting meeting notices; and the 2010 meeting schedule.

**January 19, 2010 board meeting**
Called to order at 7:06 p.m., adjourned at 8:23 p.m., with approximately 115 in the audience. The Board recognized 111 senior scholar athletes from fall sports who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average, and all-state athletes Michael Atchoo, Sean Cunningham, Brett Forman, Nathan Hicklin, Lee Keating, Michelle Moriset, and Susan Stuccheli. Actions: consent agenda (10-005); TESPA/MEA/NEA negotiating team with Jasen Witt as chief spokesperson, contract expiring June 30, 2010 (10-006); Great Start Readiness Grant acceptance of $54,400 for half-day preschool for 16 children at a per-capita allowance of $3,400 (10-007); Schools of Choice under Section 105 (10-008) and Section 105C (10-009); refusal to enter a Service Consolidation Plan with the Michigan Department of Education under MCL 388.1611D(2), which is tied to a $165 per pupil deduction (10-010); and a media center book bid for International Academy East to Follett for $36,157.54 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund (10-011).

**Curriculum (item 7)**
NASA downlink: on Monday, February 1, Troy was one of only six districts in the nation to host a live downlink with International Space Station crew, held at Athens High School, involving more than 500 students and streamed on the NASA Web site; led by science coordinator Jennifer Gottlieb. Parent survey report by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment, and Stuart Redpath: administered online with Oakland Schools from November 16 to November 23, 2009, with 2,752 surveys or 38 percent completed against a 35 percent benchmark; 65 percent of respondents gave their school a letter grade of A. Consideration to close Athens High School and Troy High School to open enrollment for 2010-2011, except not more than 25 incoming ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area, with applications February 4-19, 2010.

**Business (item 8)**
Athens Security Management System awarded to MCMI at $66,800.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund (Bid Award #9647; bids opened January 5, 2010; seven bidders invited, one responded). 2009-10 Budget Amendment Resolution appropriations:

| Fund | Amended appropriation |
| --- | --- |
| General Fund | $136,562,590 |
| Special Revenue Funds | $7,614,554 |
| Debt Service Funds | $18,749,640 |
| Capital Projects Fund | $5,032,861 |
| Internal Service Fund | $720,000 |

General Fund amended revenue is $134,482,817 against an approved $138,749,029; amended expenditures $136,562,590 against an approved $137,464,242; amended ending fund balance at June 30, 2010 is $12,904,776 against an approved $14,177,638. Michael Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, also presented an updated five-year budget forecast (item 8.C, report only).

**Other and closed session**
Tim McAvoy, director of community relations, presented the Troy Matters Communications Plan on the 2010-2011 budget process, with informational meetings March 8 and March 10 at Athens High School. The Board was to resolve, under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to enter closed session on negotiations by roll call vote.
2010_001_020310regmtg.verbose:
**Meeting.** Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting, Wednesday, February 3, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; masthead 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

**Recognitions.** North Central Association accreditation by the Advanced Accreditation Commission; Stu Redpath, chair of the districtwide NCA process, accepts the plaque. The Troy Academy of Learning Leaders (TALL), in its second year with 14 teacher leaders in monthly training, mentoring, readings, and job shadowing, won the 2009 "Best Practices in Human Resources" award from the Michigan Association of School Personnel Administrators (MASPA), presented to Jasen Witt, assistant superintendent for human resources, at the December MASPA annual conference.

**Organizational meeting minutes.** Header reads "ORGANIZATIONAL MINUTES JANUARY 26, 2010"; the footer and agenda say January 19, 2010. President Underwood called order at 7:03 p.m.; present were Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Pochodylo, Underwood, Superintendent Fowler, administrators Adamczyk, Bryan, Cottone, Davisson, Machesky, McAvoy, Mull, Witt, and approximately 115 audience members. Resolution 10-001 (Pochodylo / Edmunds) named Michael M. Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent-Business Services, Treasurer for the 2010 calendar year; 10-002 (Fleming / Hauff) continued the Superintendent of Schools as Deputy Secretary; 10-003 (Miletti / Fleming) designated Shelly Carrier, Secretary to the Superintendent, for posting meeting notices; 10-004 (Edmunds / Philippart) adopted the 2010 meeting schedule. All Yes 7, No 0. Adjourned 7:06 p.m.; submitted by Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary.

**January 19, 2010 board meeting minutes.** Order at 7:06 p.m.; present were Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Pochodylo, Underwood, Superintendent Fowler, administrators Adamczyk, Bryan, Cottone, Davisson, Jolly, Machesky, McAvoy, Mull, Stromayer, VanDenBerghe, Witt, and approximately 115 audience members. The Board recognized 111 senior scholar athletes from fall sports holding a 3.5 cumulative grade point average across cross country, boys' tennis, girls' volleyball, soccer, football, girls' swimming, girls' golf, water polo, and fall cheerleading; all-state athletes were Michael Atchoo (cross country), Sean Cunningham (boys' soccer), Brett Forman (boys' tennis), Nathan Hicklin (boys' soccer), Lee Keating (boys' tennis), Michelle Moriset (cross country), and Susan Stuccheli (volleyball). For National School Board Recognition month the Board was honored with a slide show featuring Boulan Park Middle School students.

Resolution 10-005 (Hauff / Fleming) approved consent items A-F: minutes of the December 1, 2009 meeting, December 8, 2009 workshop, January 6, 2010 special meeting, January 11, 2010 special meeting and special workshop, and the Treasurer's Report for November and December 2009 (Ayes 7, No 0). Resolution 10-006 (Pochodylo / Edmunds) named Jasen Witt chief spokesperson with Michael Adamczyk, Richard Machesky, Mondo Belardi, Gary Wood, Linda Hannon, and Bonnie Lobert for TESPA/MEA/NEA negotiations, that contract expiring June 30, 2010. Dr. Don Van Den Berghe, principal of Wass Elementary School, gave enrollment projections; Mrs. Jennifer Gottlieb, science and math coordinator, reported on the NASA downlink, Troy being Michigan's only community and one of six nationally selected.

Resolution 10-007 (Philippart / Miletti) accepted the Great Start Readiness Grant under Sections 32d and 37 through 40 and Section 38 of the State School Aid Act: an allocation of $54,400 for fiscal year 2009-2010 for a readiness program for 16 children. The district certified $-0- for full-day preschool at the approved per-capita allowance of $6,600, $-0- for comprehensive parent involvement programs, and $54,400 for half-day preschool for 16 eligible four-year-olds at the approved per-capita allowance of $3,400; more than fifty percent of enrolled children will meet income eligibility guidelines, and unallocated funds are redistributed to other eligible districts. Resolutions 10-008 (Fleming / Miletti) and 10-009 (Edmunds / Philippart) exercised Sections 105 and 105C of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, accepting applications for a limited Schools of Choice program for 2010/2011 for nonresident kindergarten and first grade students within Oakland County, and for such students from districts in a county whose intermediate school district is contiguous with the Oakland Intermediate School District. Resolution 10-010 (Pochodylo / Hauff) recited that MCL 388.1611D(2) requires an agreement with the Michigan Department of Education no later than February 1, 2010 to apply the $165 per pupil deduction in 2009-10 State School Aid revenue against an unprotected categorical other than Section 22b, and resolved that Troy will not enter such an agreement to develop a Service Consolidation Plan. Resolution 10-011 (Philippart / Edmunds) awarded media center books for International Academy East to Follett for $36,157.54 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund. Each passed Ayes 7, No 0.

Andrew Michail, Troy High School student representative, reported more than $4,000 raised for the tragedy in Haiti and the Sadie's Dance on February 20, 2010 themed "All You Need is Love." Dr. Fowler noted Maestro Leonard Slatkin of the Detroit Symphony Orchestra would work with the Troy High School band in the Athens High School auditorium on February 2, 2010 at "Night with the Stars," 7:00 p.m., free admission. Adjourned 8:23 p.m.

**January 22, 2010 board retreat.** Order at 6:00 p.m., Administrative Center, with Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Dr. Fowler, Adamczyk, Davisson, Machesky, Mull, McAvoy, Redpath, Witt, and two audience members. Topics: Public Communication; Results of Parent Survey; "TSD Matters" Update; Finance (Budget Projections, 2010/2011 Budget); Communication Plan for Budget Reductions. Adjourned 10:10 p.m.

**NASA downlink (7.A).** On Monday, February 1, Troy was one of only six districts in the nation to host a live downlink with International Space Station crew. Held at Athens High School, it anchored science activities involving more than 500 students, aired into classrooms districtwide and streamed live on the NASA Web site, credited to science coordinator Jennifer Gottlieb.

**Open enrollment (7.C).** Athens and Troy High School have been closed to open enrollment for the past two years; Troy High has maintained optimal enrollment and unexpected demographic shifts made limited Athens openings appropriate. The resolution closes both to open enrollment for 2010-2011 except not more than 25 ninth graders living in the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens; students with siblings at Athens currently in grades 9-11 may open enroll. Applications February 4-19, 2010.

Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077, to Michael Adamczyk records Bid Award #9647: bids opened January 5, 2010, only one bid anticipated given system requirements. Mr. M. Belardi, Director of Maintenance, recommended award to MCMI at $66,800.00 as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund.

**Budget forecast (8.C).** Noting that, like all Michigan school districts, Troy has struggled to balance its annual budget amid flat or insufficient revenue growth from the State of Michigan, Michael Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, was to present an updated five-year forecast; the item required no action and the forecast slides are not rendered in the extracted text.

**Troy Matters Communications Plan (9.A).** Presented February 3, 2010 by Tim McAvoy, director of community relations, to inform the community on the 2010-2011 budget process and the reductions needed to address severe cuts in state aid. Process to date: the Troy Matters Education process, TSD Focus Groups, information on school aid cuts, and legislative contacts. Vehicles include E-News, the Web site, school newsletters, social media, e-mail distribution lists, legislative outreach, Perspectives, the Troy Times staff newsletter, media, TS-TV, superintendents' updates and columns, board meeting presentations, School Finance 101, realtors, RSS feeds, student publications, advocacy avenues, presentations as requested, and informational meetings. Informational meetings were set for March 8 and March 10 at Athens High School with three main presentations and breakout sessions. Closing points: information will be evolving, Troy is not alone in this struggle, the district will keep working with state lawmakers, and Troy is a district with high expectations.

**Closed session (10.A).** The Board was to resolve, as permitted by the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to go into closed session on negotiations by roll call vote of Pochodylo, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, and Philippart, with no further business other than adjournment.
